title: Ospemifene
overview: Taking ospemifene may increase the risk that you will develop endometrial cancer (cancer of the lining of the uterus). Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had cancer or if you have abnormal vaginal bleeding. Your doctor will probably tell you not to take ospemifene. If you have any unusual vaginal bleeding while you are taking ospemifene call your doctor immediately.

sections.Before taking ospemifene,: tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this drug, any part of this drug, or any other drugs, foods or substances. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about the allergy and what symptoms you had.tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take while taking ospemifene. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.the following nonprescription or herbal products may interact with ospemifene: St. John's Wort. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking these medications before you start taking ospemifene. Do not start any of these medications while taking ospemifene without discussing with your healthcare provider.tell your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. Ospemifene may cause fetal harm. If you become pregnant while taking ospemifene, call your doctor immediately.if you are having surgery, including dental surgery, or will be on bed rest, tell the doctor or dentist you are taking ospemifene.
sections.Ospemifene may cause side effects. Tell: hot flashes or flushesvaginal dischargemuscle spasmsincreased sweating
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: hives, rash; itching; hoarseness; difficulty swallowing or breathing; or swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips or eyes Ospemifene may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
